title: Normal text contrast ≥ 4.5:1
summary: All normal text must meet WCAG AA 4.5:1 (antislop R-25; antislop-human 'Low-Contrast Text'; Claude design-system-prompt contrast chapter; pa11y audits WCAG2AA by default). Light grey text on white is the most common miss.

source.rule: R-25 Color Contrast (4.5:1 normal text)
Low-Contrast Text (compute the ratio, do not eyeball)
Contrast (WCAG): normal text under 18px minimum 4.5:1
Automated accessibility testing; WCAG2AA default standard
Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

notes: Contrast is local: test every spot text passes over, including over images and gradients. Use the WCAG formula ((L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05)) or a checker; never eyeball.

title: Large text contrast ≥ 3:1
summary: Large text (18px+ bold or 24px+ regular) needs only 3:1 per WCAG AA (antislop R-25; Claude design-system-prompt; Hallmark gate 40 thresholds).

params.window: large text pair (>=18px bold or >=24px regular)

source.rule: R-25 (large text 18px+ minimum 3:1)
Large text (18px+ bold or 24px+): minimum 3:1
Gate 40 contrast thresholds (large text WCAG 3:1)

title: Non-text UI contrast ≥ 3:1
summary: Component boundaries, icons, input borders, focus indicators, and status indicators need 3:1 against adjacent colors (WCAG 1.4.11; antislop-human 'Non-Text Contrast'; Claude design-system-prompt UI components 3:1; Hallmark gate 40 includes focus rings at 3:1).

source.rule: Non-Text Contrast (3:1, WCAG 1.4.11)
UI components (buttons, icons): minimum 3:1
Gate 40 (icons and focus rings need WCAG 3:1)
Non-Text Contrast (3:1 minimum) - UI components: buttons, inputs, checkboxes, toggles, cards; the component boundary must have 3:1 against adjacent colors

title: No contrast claims without computation
summary: The grey-on-grey hallucination: claiming a pairing passes AA without running the math (antislop-human). '#555555 on black is 2.8:1 — it fails'; the eye overestimates contrast on grey pairs and agents repeat the claim because it sounds plausible.

source.rule: The Grey-on-Grey Hallucination

tests.label: uncomputed claim fails
tests.input: This #555555 on black easily passes AA contrast.

tests.label: computed verdict passes
tests.input: #777777 on white is 4.48:1, which fails the 4.5:1 threshold for normal text.

notes: Never assert a pairing passes; run the contrast checker or the formula. #555555 on black computes to 2.8:1.

title: Text over photo/gradient: verify the worst spot
summary: White text over an image or gradient that is light in some areas drops below 4.5:1 where the image is light; checking one bright spot only is the tell (antislop-human 'Text Over a Photo or Gradient'; antislop R-25 requires testing the whole area).

source.rule: Text Over a Photo or Gradient / R-25 (test the whole area, not one point)

tests.label: single-spot check fails
tests.input: White headline over a hero photo, contrast verified only at the dark corner.

tests.label: scrim + worst spot passes
tests.input: Headline over a scrim; verified the lightest part of the image still clears 4.5:1.

title: Never remove the focus outline
summary: `outline: none` or `outline: 0` with no replacement focus style removes the only keyboard visibility indicator; banned by antislop R-32, antislop-human, and the Claude design-system-prompt ('one of the most common accessibility failures').

source.rule: R-32 Keyboard Accessibility (FORBIDDEN outline: none without replacement)
Removed Focus Outline
Never remove the focus ring; replace it with :focus-visible
An `outline: none` or `focus:outline-none` with no visible replacement leaves sighted keyboard users with no way to see where they are

title: Focus indicator must be visible and 3:1
summary: A focus ring the same color as the background, one that only appears on hover, or one thinner than a 1px border fails the contrast bar (antislop-human 'Weak or Invisible Focus Indicator'); Hallmark gate 26 requires :focus-visible, :active, and :disabled styling on every interactive element.

source.rule: Weak or Invisible Focus Indicator (R-32, R-34)
Gate 26: interactive element lacks :focus-visible / :active / :disabled

tests.label: invisible focus fails
tests.input: button:focus { outline-color: #FFFFFF; } /* white ring on a white page */

notes: Check the indicator in every theme you ship, light and dark (R-34). Focus rings must also appear instantly — no fade-in (Hallmark gate 15).

title: No mouse-only interactions
summary: Menus that open on hover only, dropdowns that click-open but do not keyboard-open, drag-and-drop with no keyboard fallback: each excludes keyboard and assistive-tech users (antislop-human 'Mouse-Only Patterns'; Claude design-system-prompt keyboard navigation; antislop R-32).

source.rule: Mouse-Only Patterns (R-32)
Keyboard navigation: everything reachable and operable by keyboard; hover-only interactions fail
Enforce a clickable non-interactive element has at least one keyboard event listener.

tests.label: hover-only menu fails
tests.input: Dropdown opens on :hover only; Enter/Space do nothing when the trigger is focused.

tests.label: keyboard-operable passes
tests.input: Dropdown opens on click or Enter/Space and navigates with arrow keys; Esc closes it.

title: Logical tab order; dialogs close on Escape
summary: Focus that jumps around, skips content, or lands on hidden elements because DOM order does not match visual order makes navigation unpredictable (antislop-human 'Broken Tab Order'); modals must close on Escape (Claude design-system-prompt; antislop R-32).

source.rule: Broken Tab Order (R-32)
Modals must close on Escape; tab order must be logical
Escape dismisses whatever opened last: tooltip, then menu, then dialog; native `<dialog>` with `showModal()` closes on Escape

tests.label: scattered tabindex fails
tests.input: tabindex="5" on the footer link, tabindex="1" on a hidden sidebar — focus jumps past main content.

tests.label: source-order passes
tests.input: DOM order matches visual order; skip link jumps to main; modal traps focus and closes on Escape.

notes: Never give real content tabindex="-1" unless part of a controlled focus trap such as a dialog.

title: Interactive hit targets ≥ 44px
summary: Tap/click targets smaller than 44px × 44px exclude touch and low-precision users (antislop R-03 minimum tap target 44px; Claude design-system-prompt 'interactive hit targets: never smaller than 44px × 44px').

source.rule: R-03 (button sizes meet the minimum tap target 44px)
Interactive hit targets: never smaller than 44px × 44px
Aim for 44x44px on touch and 40x40px on desktop where density permits. WCAG 2.5.8's Level AA baseline is a 24x24 CSS-pixel target, or one of its exceptions
Ensure touch targets have sufficient size and space

title: No color-only status feedback
summary: Success/error/status communicated only by color excludes color-blind and low-vision users and disappears in forced-colors mode (antislop-human 'Color-Only Feedback'; Claude design-system-prompt 'don't rely on color alone to communicate state').

source.rule: Color-Only Feedback (C-4)
Don't rely on color alone to communicate state — pair with icons, text, or position
Status needs a redundant cue: an icon, text or an underline alongside the color (1.4.1)

tests.label: red border only fails
tests.input: input.invalid { border-color: red; } /* no message, no icon */

tests.label: text-first error passes
tests.input: "Password must be at least 8 characters" shown beside the red-bordered field.

title: Motion must have a prefers-reduced-motion fallback
summary: Every animation/transition needs a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) alternative (Claude design-system-prompt Motion; Hallmark gate 27: any transform/animation keyframe not covered by the fallback fails).

source.rule: Respect prefers-reduced-motion
Gate 27: every transform/animation keyframe covered by prefers-reduced-motion
Wrap motion in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` so it is opt-in

tests.label: uncovered animation fails
tests.input: .card { transition: transform 0.3s ease; } /* no reduced-motion media query in the stylesheet */

title: Use semantic HTML, not div-on-click
summary: Buttons are <button>, links are <a>, structure uses <nav>/<main>/<article>; ARIA is a patch for when semantic HTML can't express the role (Claude design-system-prompt 'Semantic HTML'; pa11y/axe audits flag role misuse).

source.rule: Semantic HTML: <button> for buttons, never <div onclick>; proper heading hierarchy
Runs axe-core / HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG audits
Enforce that non-interactive, visible elements (such as `<div>`) that have click handlers use the role attribute.

notes: Also covers heading hierarchy: don't skip levels (<h1> to <h3>).

title: Alt text on meaningful images
summary: Every meaningful image needs descriptive alt text; decorative images get alt=""; missing alt fails screen-reader and automated audits (Claude design-system-prompt screen-reader support; pa11y example: 'Img element is the only content of the link, but is missing alt text').

source.rule: Alt text on every meaningful image; empty alt for decorative
Audits alt-text violations (HTML_CodeSniffer example result)
Ensure elements have alternative text or a role of none or presentation
Enforce all elements that require alternative text have meaningful information to relay back to end user.
Images must have accessible names unless they are decorative or redundant

tests.label: descriptive alt passes

notes: Decorative images use alt="" so screen readers skip them.

title: Labels on every form input
summary: Placeholder text is not a label — it disappears when the user types (Claude design-system-prompt form design; 'labels on every form input').

source.rule: Labels on every form input; placeholder is not a label
Ensure every form element has a label
Each form control must have an associated label

tests.label: placeholder-only fails
tests.input: <input placeholder="Email address"> with no <label for> or aria-label.

notes: Use type="email"/"tel" and autocomplete attributes for mobile keyboards and autofill.

title: Text must reflow at 200% zoom
summary: Fixed pixel font sizes and overflow:hidden containers that clip text at 200% zoom break WCAG 1.4.4 text resizing (antislop-human 'Text That Cannot Zoom', R-35).

source.rule: Text That Cannot Zoom (WCAG 1.4.4, R-35)

tests.label: clipped at zoom fails
tests.input: body { font-size: 12px; } .copy { overflow: hidden; height: 200px; } /* text clips at 200% zoom */

tests.label: fluid type passes
tests.input: body { font-size: clamp(16px, 1rem + 0.5vw, 20px); } /* reflows at 200% zoom on a narrow viewport */

title: Focus indicator at least 2px or equivalent area
summary: A custom focus indicator thinner than 2px — outline: 1px, outline: thin — fails the visible-area bar for keyboard users (better-accessibility: 'Use at least a 2px solid perimeter or an equivalent visible area'; WCAG 2.4.7 minimum 2px per wcag-accessibility-audit).

source.rule: Visible Focus Rings — at least 2px solid perimeter or equivalent visible area
Focus rings — custom outline: 2px solid; never thinner
2.4.7 Focus Visible — minimum 2px, high contrast

notes: Works with ZS-A11Y-006 (never outline: none) and ZS-A11Y-007 (the ring's contrast must be verified against every adjacent color). A 2px+ outline is the floor; verify the complete indicator in every theme, including forced-colors mode.

title: sr-only must hide visually, not from assistive tech
summary: An .sr-only / .visually-hidden class implemented with display: none or visibility: hidden removes the content from assistive tech entirely — the pattern hides from everyone (better-accessibility screen-readers: 'Never use display:none or visibility:hidden for this; both remove the content from assistive tech entirely').

source.rule: Visually hidden content — canonical .sr-only pattern; never display:none or visibility:hidden

tests.label: canonical clip pattern passes
tests.input: .sr-only { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; border: 0; }

notes: Use 1px boxes, not 0 — some screen readers skip zero-sized elements. white-space: nowrap prevents words from being read as one run-together string. Skip links add a focus variant that un-hides the element (:focus overrides the positioning).

title: Autoplaying media needs visible controls
summary: Media that moves, blinks, or updates automatically for more than 5 seconds needs a visible pause/stop control (WCAG 2.2.2); muted looping hero videos included (better-accessibility motion-and-zoom: 'No autoplaying media without visible controls').

source.rule: No autoplaying media without visible controls (WCAG 2.2.2)
2.2.2 auto-playing media with controls
Ensure <video> or <audio> elements do not autoplay audio for more than 3 seconds without a control mechanism to stop or mute the audio

notes: Under prefers-reduced-motion, kill autoplay entirely and start carousels paused. Media without sound that runs longer than 5 seconds still needs the pause control — duration is the trigger, not audio.

title: Auto-dismiss timers need a 5-second floor
summary: Auto-dismissing toasts that time out in under 5 seconds give users no window to act; 5 seconds is the floor, and hovering or focusing the toast must pause the timer (better-accessibility motion-and-zoom: 'If a toast must time out, 5 seconds is the floor').

source.rule: Autoplay and timed UI — 5 second floor; hover/focus pauses the timer

notes: Flags dismiss-style timers under 5000ms. Not every setTimeout is a dismissal timer — review hits in context. Low-stakes confirmations may auto-dismiss; anything containing an action, an error, or information the user may need to act on stays until dismissed.

title: Toasts need a live region to announce
summary: A toast with no aria-live or role is invisible to screen readers — the only way to convey the information fails (fixing-accessibility: 'toasts must not be the only way to convey critical information'; better-accessibility: toasts belong in a polite role="status" live region).

source.rule: Toasts must not be the only way to convey critical information
Announce Dynamic Content — polite live region (role="status") for toasts
Live regions — role="status" for toasts, role="alert" for urgent errors

notes: Default to polite (role="status"); reserve role="alert" / aria-live="assertive" for urgent errors not tied to a control. The 'only path to an action inside an auto-dismissing toast' variant — data loss on a schedule — is semantic and deferred to M3.

title: Placeholder is not a label
summary: An input with placeholder= but no accessible name attribute leaves the field unlabeled — placeholder text disappears the moment the user types (better-accessibility forms: 'A placeholder is never a label'; fixing-accessibility: every input must be labeled).

source.rule: Labels — placeholder is never a label
Every input, select, and textarea must be labeled

notes: The regex inspects the input element only; a linked <label for> or wrapping label also satisfies but is a cross-element association (see semantic ZS-A11Y-015). Placeholders used in addition to a label are fine and show an example of the expected format.

title: No fixed min-width blocking 320px reflow
summary: A fixed min-width of 800px or more on a container forces horizontal scrolling at the 320px equivalent (400% zoom on a 1280px viewport), breaking WCAG 1.4.10 reflow — content must work with vertical scrolling only (better-accessibility motion-and-zoom; wcag-accessibility-audit 1.4.10).

source.rule: Reflow at 320px — no two-dimensional scrolling
1.4.10 Reflow — content reflows to 320px width without horizontal scrolling

notes: min-width is the blocker; max-width is fine. Genuinely two-dimensional content (tables, maps, code blocks) scrolls inside its own container — that is the 2D-content exception, not a page-level min-width. Fixed heights on text containers are the same failure mode under 200% zoom: prefer min-height.

title: No forced-color-adjust: none without system colors
summary: forced-color-adjust: none freezes the authored color in Windows High Contrast mode, defeating the user's forced-colors palette (better-accessibility focus-and-keyboard: 'never freeze the authored color with forced-color-adjust: none unless the control remains perceivable').

source.rule: Forced-colors — keep default color adjustment or use a system color such as Highlight

notes: In forced-colors: active, keep the default color adjustment or explicitly use a system color (Highlight, ButtonText, CanvasText). Custom focus colors must be re-verified under forced colors, not frozen.

title: No positive tabindex values
summary: Positive tabindex hijacks the tab order for the whole page, jumping focus past content in DOM order; only tabindex="0" (join natural order) and tabindex="-1" (programmatic focus) are valid (better-accessibility focus-and-keyboard: 'Positive tabindex: never. It hijacks the tab order for the whole page; fix the DOM order instead').

source.rule: tabindex rules — only 0 and -1, never positive values
Do not use tabindex greater than 0
Elements should not have tabindex greater than zero
Enforce `tabIndex` value is not greater than zero.

notes: Concrete, machine-checkable half of the semantic broken-tab-order rule (ZS-A11Y-009): fix the DOM order instead of patching with positive values. Roving tabindex for composite widgets: active item 0, all others -1.

title: Never aria-hidden a focusable element
summary: aria-hidden="true" on a focusable element creates tab stops that don't exist for screen readers — elements you can Tab to that are invisible to assistive tech (better-accessibility: 'Never put it on (or above) a focusable element; that creates stops you can Tab to that don't exist for a screen reader').

source.rule: Never put aria-hidden on (or above) a focusable element
aria-hidden — never on a focusable element
ARIA hidden element must not be focusable or contain focusable elements
Disallow `aria-hidden="true"` from being set on focusable elements.
A hidden element should not contain any tabbable elements

notes: If you hide something interactive, also remove it from the tab order (and from focusability). Decorative elements get aria-hidden="true" only when they are genuinely non-focusable.

title: No aria-label on role-less div or span
summary: aria-label on a plain <div> or <span> is ignored by most screen readers — names on non-interactive, role-less elements do nothing (better-accessibility semantics-and-aria: 'Names on non-interactive, role-less elements are ignored by most screen readers').

source.rule: Common ARIA mistakes — aria-label on a plain div or span

notes: aria-label only works on elements with a role or native naming. The real fix is usually a native element — <button>, <a>, <nav> — rather than ARIA on a div.

title: Icon-only buttons need accessible names
summary: An icon-only button with no aria-label or aria-labelledby has no accessible name — screen readers announce nothing or read the file name (fixing-accessibility: 'icon-only buttons must have aria-label or aria-labelledby'; better-accessibility: 'Icon-only buttons need a descriptive aria-label').

source.rule: Icon-only buttons must have aria-label or aria-labelledby
Accessible Names Everywhere — icon-only buttons need a descriptive aria-label
Ensure buttons have discernible text

notes: The icon inside a labeled button should be aria-hidden="true" so the name isn't doubled. A visible text label inside the button also satisfies the rule (text-first buttons don't match this pattern); aria-labelledby pointing at a visible label works too.

title: Viewport meta must not block zoom
summary: `maximum-scale=1` and `user-scalable=no` switch pinch-zoom off, so a low-vision user cannot enlarge the text to 200% (WCAG 1.4.4). better-accessibility bans both outright in the viewport meta.

source.rule: Never set `maximum-scale=1` or `user-scalable=no` in the viewport meta
`maximum-scale=1` or `user-scalable=no` | Remove it

notes: Only blocking values fire: maximum-scale of 2 or more and user-scalable=yes stay clean. iOS ignores user-scalable on newer versions, Android does not, so the textual ban still applies.

title: Role-based custom controls need a keyboard handler
summary: `role="button"` (or tab/menuitem/switch) on a div or span promises the full keyboard model to a screen reader, but the element only gets one if the author adds an Enter/Space handler. A role with no key handler is worse than no role at all.

source.rule: `role="button"` or `role="tab"` with no `onKeyDown` | Use the native element, or implement the APG key map
Where a native element is truly impossible, the full polyfill is `role="button"` plus `tabindex="0"` plus Enter and Space handlers

tests.label: role=button with no key handler fails
role=tab with no key handler fails

notes: Line-scoped: the whole opening tag must sit on one line. Native elements (button, input, a[href]) are deliberately out of scope; the pattern matches non-native hosts only.

title: Do not disable submit to gate validation
summary: `disabled={!isValid}` on a submit button hides why the form cannot be sent, drops focus to body for keyboard users and never announces an error. Validate on submit and focus the first invalid field instead.

source.rule: `disabled={!isValid}` on a submit button | Keep it enabled and validate on submit
Validate on submit, never by disabling submit until the form is valid
Never disable submit to gate validation. Validate on submit instead

tests.label: disabled bound to a negation fails

notes: Matches the JSX form only (disabled={...} bound to a negation). A plain HTML disabled attribute is left alone because the surrounding state is not visible to a line-scoped regex.

title: Live regions must exist before their content changes
summary: A polite live region inserted together with its message is announced inconsistently across screen readers. Render the empty `role="status"` region up front and only change its text when an update arrives.

source.rule: `{msg && <div role="status">`, region mounted with its text | Render the empty region first and update its text
For repeated polite updates, keep a stable empty region in the DOM before changing its text. Inserting a new polite region with its content is announced inconsistently

tests.label: stable region with injected text passes

notes: Detects the conditional-mount JSX shape only; a region rendered once and updated through state is the sanctioned fix. Inert in plain HTML.

title: Identity inputs need an autocomplete token
summary: A valid `autocomplete` token on fields that collect information about the user is a WCAG 1.3.5 requirement, and it is also what makes password managers and 2FA autofill work. `type="email"`, `tel` and `password` are the standard cases.

source.rule: A valid `autocomplete` token on fields about the user is a WCAG requirement (1.3.5). Pair it with a descriptive `name` attribute, a real `<form>` and no fake inputs
Add a valid `autocomplete` token and a descriptive `name` attribute, plus the `type` and `inputmode` that summon the right keyboard

notes: Line-scoped. Password inputs should carry current-password or new-password rather than off; the rule only checks that a token is present.

title: Never combine disabled with aria-disabled
summary: Native `disabled` already removes the control from the tab order and suppresses activation, while `aria-disabled="true"` only announces the state. Setting both announces a state the element no longer has, and the two mechanisms disagree on focusability.

source.rule: Never set both `disabled` and `aria-disabled` on the same element

tests.label: JSX disabled prop plus aria-disabled fails

notes: The `\sdisabled` prefix keeps aria-disabled itself from satisfying the native-attribute half of the match.

title: Infinite animation needs a pause or stop control
summary: Anything moving on its own for more than five seconds needs a visible pause, stop or hide control (WCAG 2.2.2). An animation declared `infinite` runs forever, so a marquee, float or bouncing decoration ships a 2.2.2 failure unless a control exists.

source.rule: Anything moving, blinking or updating on its own for more than 5 seconds needs a visible pause control (2.2.2)

Visible controls on anything that moves on its own (2.2.2). Anything moving, blinking or updating on its own for more than 5 seconds needs a visible pause or stop control, muted looping hero videos included

notes: Loading spinners, skeleton and progress animations are excluded by name, since motion-and-zoom keeps them under reduced motion. A two-declaration form (animation-name plus animation-iteration-count on separate lines) stays clean; the shorthand or animation-name must carry infinite on the scanned line.

title: Visible label text must appear in the accessible name (2.5.3)
summary: WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name: a control showing "Send" whose accessible name is "Submit message" breaks voice-control users, who say what they see and get nothing. Prefer visible text or aria-labelledby over aria-label, and start any aria-label with the visible words.

source.rule: WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name: a button showing "Send" with `aria-label="Submit message"` breaks voice control users who say "click Send"
Visible label text must appear in the accessible name. Decorative elements get `aria-hidden="true"`, never on a focusable element
`aria-label` whose text omits the visible label | Start the name with the visible text

tests.label: aria-label that drops the visible word fails
tests.input: <button aria-label="Submit message">Send</button> (visible text "Send" is absent from the accessible name)

tests.label: aria-label that starts with the visible word passes
icon-only button with a name passes

notes: Needs the rendered accessible name and the visible text side by side, so it is left to the triage pass rather than a regex.

title: Decorative SVG / canvas without aria-hidden or an accessible name
summary: Hallmark gate 33: a visual-only <svg>, <canvas> or decorative figure must carry aria-label (if it conveys something) or aria-hidden="true" (if it does not). Hand-built SVG illustration and CSS art are otherwise announced as an unlabelled 'group' or skipped silently - 'Skipping this is the new accessibility tell'.

source.rule: 33. Does any visual-only `<svg>`, custom-art `<div>`, `<canvas>`, or decorative figure lack `aria-label` or `aria-hidden="true"`? Hand-built CSS art and SVG illustrations need an accessible name *or* an explicit hide. Skipping this is the new accessibility tell.

tests.label: decorative svg hidden from AT passes
named canvas passes
tests.input: <canvas id="hero-canvas" role="img" aria-label="Live render of the chair in oak" width="800" height="400"></canvas>

notes: Checks the opening tag only (the ui/a11y engine scans line by line, so a multi-line React SVG needs the attribute on the first tag line). is ZS-A11Y-014, icon-only buttons ZS-A11Y-028, and aria-hidden on focusable elements ZS-A11Y-026; role="presentation"/"none" counts as an explicit hide.

title: aria-hidden plus a sequential tabindex makes an invisible tab stop
summary: aria-hidden="true" removes an element from the accessibility tree but not from the keyboard: tabindex 0 (or any positive value) on the same element leaves a focus stop that no screen reader announces. tabindex="-1" is the allowed form because it removes the element from sequential focus (axe-core aria-hidden-focus; jsx-a11y no-aria-hidden-on-focusable; IBM equal-access aria_hidden_nontabbable).

source.rule: ARIA hidden element must not be focusable or contain focusable elements
Ensure aria-hidden elements are not focusable nor contain focusable elements
Enforce that `aria-hidden="true"` is not set on focusable elements.
Fail: `<div aria-hidden="true" tabIndex="0" />` — Succeed: `<button aria-hidden="true" tabIndex="-1" />` // `tabIndex=-1` removes the element from sequential focus navigation so we don't flag it.
Element "{0}" should not be focusable within the subtree of an element with an 'aria-hidden' attribute with value 'true'

notes: Extended twin of ZS-A11Y-026, which only covers natively focusable tags (button/input/select/textarea/a[href]); this covers the tabindex-driven tab stop on any element. Negative tabindex is exempt on purpose (jsx-a11y documents tabIndex="-1" as safe). Attributes must sit on the same line as the opening tag — multi-line opening tags are not seen.

title: role must be a valid, non-abstract ARIA role
summary: A role value that is not an ARIA role — a made-up name like role="list-item", or an abstract role such as role="widget" — leaves the element with no semantics at all, so screen readers announce nothing. Match the value against the concrete role set (WAI-ARIA 1.2/1.3, DPUB-ARIA, WAI-ARIA Graphics).

source.rule: Ensure all elements with a role attribute use a valid value
Role must be one of the valid ARIA roles: ${data.values}
Abstract role cannot be directly used: ${data.values}
Enforce that elements with ARIA roles must use a valid, non-abstract ARIA role.
ARIA roles must be valid for the element to which they are assigned

notes: Role value is checked as-is, so `role="checkbox menuitem"` passes on the first token. Abstract roles (command, composite, input, landmark, range, roletype, section, sectionhead, select, structure, widget, window) are excluded from the allowlist, matching axe-core's abstractrole check. Same-line constraint as the other attribute rules.

title: Redundant role restating the element's implicit role
summary: Writing the role a native element already has (role="button" on

source.rule: Enforce explicit role property is not the same as implicit/default role property on element.
Fail: `
The default options for this rule allow an implicit role of `navigation` to be applied to a `nav` element as is advised by w3.

`<button>` -- never add `role="button"`; `<a href>` -- never add `role="link"`; `<input type="checkbox">` -- never add `role="checkbox"`; `<select>` -- never add `role="listbox"` (implicit roles, redundant and can cause double announcements)

tests.label: svg role img passes (no implicit role)

notes: Pair list is deliberate, not a generic implicit-role map: nav/navigation is excluded (jsx-a11y's documented exception, and W3C advises it) and ul/list is excluded (the Safari-VoiceOver workaround). Paired lookaheads keep `<button role="link">` (a real override) from matching.

title: Not a real aria-* attribute
summary: An attribute that starts with aria- but is not a WAI-ARIA state or property (typos like aria-labeledby, inventions like aria-hidden-state) is silently ignored by the browser, so the name or state it was meant to carry never reaches assistive technology (axe-core aria-valid-attr; jsx-a11y aria-props; IBM equal-access aria_attribute_allowed).

source.rule: Ensure attributes that begin with aria- are valid ARIA attributes
Invalid ARIA attribute name: ${data.values}

Elements cannot use an invalid ARIA attribute. This will fail if it finds an `aria-*` property that is not listed in WAI-ARIA States and Properties spec. Fail: `<input aria-labeledby="address_label">`
Enforce all `aria-*` props are valid.
The attribute(s) '{0}' referenced by the element <{1}> is not a valid ARIA state or property

notes: Allowlist is axe-core lib/standards/aria-attrs.js (52 names, ARIA 1.2+1.3). A future ARIA attribute added upstream will read as invalid until the list is refreshed — refresh it when the axe-core reference is re-synced.

title: Invalid ARIA state or property value
summary: ARIA states take specific token values; a truthy-looking value (aria-expanded="1", aria-hidden="yes", aria-live="true", aria-haspopup="yes") is invalid, so the state is dropped and the widget never announces open/closed or hidden. Values must come from the attribute's own value set (jsx-a11y aria-proptypes; axe-core aria-valid-attr-value; IBM equal-access aria_attribute_value_valid).

source.rule: Enforce ARIA state and property values are valid.
Ensure all ARIA attributes have valid values
The value "{0}" specified for attribute '{1}' on element <{2}> is not valid
ARIA property values must be valid

notes: Covers the boolean states plus live/current/orientation/sort/autocomplete/haspopup/invalid. JSX braces are handled (`aria-hidden={true}` passes), so only literal wrong values fire. aria-relevant, aria-dropeffect and aria-grabbed are left out (multi-token/complex value spaces).

title: ARIA widget role missing its required state
summary: Widget roles require their state attribute: checkbox/radio/switch/menuitemcheckbox/menuitemradio need aria-checked, slider/spinbutton/meter need aria-valuenow, combobox needs aria-expanded, heading needs aria-level. Without it the widget announces as a nameless box and never reports its state (axe-core aria-required-attr; jsx-a11y role-has-required-aria-props).

source.rule: Ensure elements with ARIA roles have all required ARIA attributes
Required ARIA attribute not present: ${data.values}
requiredAttrs: ['aria-checked'] for checkbox/radio/menuitemcheckbox/menuitemradio/switch, ['aria-valuenow'] for slider/spinbutton/meter, ['aria-expanded'] for combobox, ['aria-level'] for heading
Elements with ARIA roles must have all required attributes for that role. Fail: `` — the checkbox role requires the aria-checked state

tests.label: checkbox with aria-checked passes
tests.input: Enable two-factor auth

notes: Roles and required attributes come from axe-core lib/standards/aria-roles.js, so option/tab (aria-selected) are deliberately absent — axe does not list them. Only the attribute on the same opening tag counts; axe resolves inheritance through idrefs and would additionally flag those cases.

title: iframe or frame with no accessible name
summary: A frame with no title (or an empty one) is announced as "frame" with no destination, so screen-reader users cannot tell which embed they are entering. Every iframe/frame needs a non-empty title, aria-label or aria-labelledby (axe-core frame-title; jsx-a11y iframe-has-title; IBM equal-access frame_title_exists).

source.rule: Frames must have an accessible name
Ensure <iframe> and <frame> elements have an accessible name
Enforce iframe elements have a title attribute.
Inline frames must have a unique, non-empty 'title' attribute; Fail: Inline frame does not have a 'title' attribute

notes: axe accepts four alternatives (non-empty title, aria-label, aria-labelledby, presentational role) — all four are honoured here. Title/aria-label must be on the same line as the opening tag; a prettier-formatted multi-line iframe will read as untitled.

title: List element with a non-<li> child
summary: <ul> and <ol> may only directly contain <li>, <script> or <template>; a <div>/<a>/text sibling breaks the list, and screen readers stop announcing item counts. Generated card/step lists routinely wrap <div> items in <ol> (axe-core list / only-listitems; IBM equal-access list_children_valid).

source.rule: <ul> and <ol> must only directly contain <li>, <script> or <template> elements
List element has direct children that are not allowed: ${data.values}
List component with "group" role must limit children to <listitem> elements; Fail: List component with "group" role has children that are not <listitem> elements

notes: The child must start on the same line as the <ul>/<ol> open tag (the ui/a11y engine scans line by line); a pretty-printed list whose first <div> sits on the next line is not detected. Parentage rules for <li>/<dt>/<dd> (axe listitem/dlitem) need a document pass — see featureIdeas.

title: Anchor used as a button (href="#" / javascript: / onClick only)
summary: <a href="#"> and <a href="javascript:void(0)"> announce as links and activate on Enter only, so an action wearing link semantics confuses both keyboard and screen-reader users; an <a> with a click handler and no href is not focusable at all. Actions belong on <button> (jsx-a11y anchor-is-valid).

source.rule: Enforce all anchors are valid, navigable elements.
All these anchor implementations indicate that the element is only used to execute JavaScript code: `Perform action` `Perform action` `Perform action` — All the above should be replaced with: ``

notes: In-page anchors (`href="#pricing"`) and real hrefs with a click handler are left alone. Covers the two unambiguous jsx-a11y cases: placeholder/javascript href, and a clickable anchor with no href.

title: autofocus steals focus on load
summary: Autofocusing on load drops the caret into a field the user did not choose: screen-reader and keyboard users are teleported past the page, and magnifier users lose their place. Set focus programmatically only where the user expects it (dialog open, validation error) — never with the autofocus/autoFocus attribute (jsx-a11y no-autofocus).

source.rule: Enforce that `autoFocus` prop is either not set at all on elements or is only set to `false`. Auto-focusing elements can cause usability issues for sighted and non-sighted users, alike.
Fail: `<div autoFocus />` `<div autoFocus="true" />` `<div autoFocus={undefined} />`; Succeed: `<div />` `<div autoFocus="false" />`

tests.label: no autofocus passes
tests.input: <input type="search" name="q" placeholder="Search docs" aria-label="Search docs" />

notes: Matches `autofocus` and `autoFocus` case-insensitively, and honours the documented escape hatch `autoFocus="false"` / `autoFocus={false}`. Dialog focus management done in code (ref.focus() on open) is out of scope — this rule only sees the attribute.

title: New-tab link with no rel and no advance warning
summary: A link that opens a new tab or window must warn the user in advance (WCAG 3.2.2 / G201) and should carry rel="noopener noreferrer". IBM's rule fires on `a[target]` without "new window"/"new tab" in the text, title or aria-describedby; the mechanical half is a missing or non-noopener rel (IBM equal-access a_target_warning).

source.rule: Users should be warned in advance if their input action will open a new window
Inform the user when their input action will open a new window
context: "dom:a[target],dom:area[target],dom:base[target]" ... passed = tStr == "_parent" || tStr == "_self" || tStr == "_top" ... textStr.indexOf("new window") / "new tab"

Adding rel="noopener noreferrer" always satisfies it; the human half (visible "(opens in a new tab)" text or title) stays a human rule.
